artifacts.body:
# ISSUE-26 implementation plan

Add a completion-gated connection to the Observer hub. The connection opens a local DEEP FIELD terminal with handle selection, a message index, the archived Keel farewell, a scripted SYSOP greeting, and a return to the hub. Use the detailed execution profile for the approved multi-area work. The existing content, save, and scene APIs make a single claim feasible. Estimate 6–12 hours for implementation and focused validation within the 32-hour claim budget, with browser runtime evidence supplied by the existing PR workflow.

## What we know

- Chapter 2 supplies the five banner lines and their order, preserves Keel's March 1 farewell, and describes SYSOP as a local preservation routine. The farewell already exists as `lore.last-sysop` with its title, author, date, and body in JSON. [Design](../../docs/game-design.md#chapter-2-the-deferred-line) · [Archive record](../../content/archives/lore-last-sysop.json)
- `createGame.completeEpisodes` grants the completion fact, assigns a designation on first completion, and persists on a successful attempt. `factsOf` reconstructs completion from saved `episodes`. The existing v1 fixture has the completed episode, a designation, and FORGE flags. The migration test checks that all these survive loading. `src/puzzle/game.ts:51`, `src/puzzle/game.ts:83`, `src/progress/save.ts:213`, `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json:7`, `tests/unit/save.test.ts:91`.
- `showHub` is shared by startup and the ending, and creates the hub with a `buildTools` callback. That callback is evaluated on mount and refresh. A terminal menu item already accepts both a click and its typed number or label. `src/main.ts:104`, `src/app/tools.ts:145`, `src/app/hub.ts:19`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts:56`.
- Save schema v2 already has a normalized nullable profile handle and an explicit v0/v1 migration. `openSaveSession` exposes boolean writes and protects unsupported saves. `src/progress/save.ts:29`, `src/progress/save.ts:149`, `src/progress/save.ts:180`, `src/progress/save.ts:204`.
- Browser and Node content readers already discover all JSON. The shared loader classifies by directory, reports file and field errors, and feeds the manifest, CLI, and Vite build. Nested reference checks belong in `checkReferences`. `src/content/browser.ts:3`, `src/content/node.ts:6`, `src/content/validate.ts:42`, `src/content/validate.ts:149`, `scripts/validate-content.ts:5`, `scripts/content-plugin.ts:11`.
- The `Browser tests` workflow runs the Playwright test directory against a production build. Its existing fixture serves the Pages subpath by request interception. The planner sandbox has no usable browser profile. `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:21`, `playwright.config.ts:5`, `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3`.

## What we're assuming

- A returning caller can reopen the board from the hub and choose an identity again. Prefill the saved handle and show read markers in the message index after login. The reload and reconnect browser journey will check that this is discoverable.
- Use the selected identity as the saved handle whichever login path the player chooses. Keep the existing designation available as its own choice. A supported completed save can structurally lack a designation because the field is nullable. Check that custom login remains available in that case. `src/progress/save.ts:24`, `src/progress/save.ts:37`.
- The BBS board indexes selected Archive records by ID. One Archive JSON entry and one board-index reference are sufficient to publish another message. The temporary-copy test will exercise that complete authoring path.

## Open questions

- Whether the banner, hints, and all three message treatments fit and remain readable with keyboard navigation on a narrow viewport requires a rendered build. The button journey and a narrow-viewport check in the browser plan cover this.
- Whether a hosted runner has Chromium and produces passing journey evidence is unknown during planning. The tester can verify spec discovery and source wiring locally. The existing `Browser tests` workflow supplies runtime evidence.

## Architectural context

Episode completion already has a durable fact, and the hub already has one dispatch path for typed menu labels and clicks. The missing pieces are a board offer built from that fact, a BBS scene with its own session, and save-backed identity and read state. Keep the boundaries at content validation, pure BBS logic, the BBS view, and app scene wiring. The existing Episode 000 progression and FORGE paths can stay independent of the board.

## Implementation sequence

1. **Add authored board content.** Create `content/bbs/relay-07.json` with an ID, board title, required condition `completed:episode.000`, banner, messages, and SYSOP greeting. Store the exact five lines at `docs/game-design.md:99` in order. The first message points to `lore.last-sysop` so both views show the existing farewell from its original JSON. Author the greeting in the terse voice of the preservation routine, with no new claim about Keel or other callers. Put fixed command labels and syntax hints in the interface. Add a short authoring entry in `docs/content-authoring.md` describing the message reference and the existing content validation command.
2. **Register and validate the board.** In `src/content/schema.ts`, add a strict `bbsMessageSchema` for an index entry with an `archive` ID and a strict `bbsBoardSchema` for the record. Require a nonempty message index and nonempty greeting and banner lines. Export `BbsBoard` and extend `Content` with `bbs: BbsBoard[]`. Add `bbs` to `SCHEMAS` and the initial content object in `src/content/validate.ts`. In `checkReferences`, validate `requires` and report unknown or repeated archive references at `messages.<index>.archive`. Top-level duplicate board IDs and manifest entries use the normal loader. Update `emptyContent` in `tests/unit/helpers.ts` and cover validation in `tests/unit/content.test.ts`.
3. **Add save-compatible progress.** In `src/progress/save.ts`, extract the existing handle transform as `normalizeHandle` and reuse it for profile parsing and login so the displayed and reloaded values agree, including for long Unicode input. Add `bbsReadMessages` as an additive v2 field, defaulting to an empty array when omitted. Initialize it in `freshSave` and the v0/v1 lift. Use stable, board-scoped keys of the form `<board-id>:<archive-id>`, which is unambiguous with the ID schema. Apply only BBS effects to this field or `profile.handle` and write through `openSaveSession.persist`. Keep read history distinct from the hub's archive facts and leave preferences, designation, access level, and door state under their existing owners. Extend `tests/unit/save.test.ts` for old v2 data, the initialized v1 shape, and round-trip behavior.
4. **Implement pure state and commands.** Create `src/bbs/bbs.ts` with `findBbsOffer`, `connectBbs`, and `dispatchBbs`. Use the shared condition evaluator for offer and connection checks. Resolve the board's ordered archive references against eligible archives from the game, then show the login phase. Model login, main menu, message index, and disconnected state. Accept `LOGIN <handle>` and `DESIGNATION` at login. Offer `MESSAGES`, `READ <archive-id>`, `SYSOP`, and `MENU` after login, with `HELP` and `DISCONNECT` in either phase. Parse verbs and archive IDs case-insensitively and preserve the handle's case. Return state, feedback, and explicit save changes to the caller. Invalid or unavailable actions leave progress alone and show a usable hint for the current phase. An accepted login saves the normalized identity, and opening an eligible message records its read key once. Commands and state have no DOM, network, clock, or storage access. Add public API coverage in `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts`.
5. **Build the scene using the terminal.** Create `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts` with `createBbsScene` returning the existing `Scene` contract. In `src/terminal/terminal.ts`, extend `createTerminal` with an optional prompt used for both the input label and command echo, and extend the print tones for system, historical, and SYSOP output. Use `BBS>` in the new scene and the default `OBS>` in the hub. Map the terminal commands, fixed menu buttons, custom-handle form, and message buttons to the same BBS dispatcher. Render the per-phase hints beside the controls, including the current command syntax. Use the generic terminal panel for the handle form and dynamic message buttons so an authored title cannot shadow a command. Label transcript blocks `SYSTEM`, `HISTORICAL MESSAGE`, and `SYSOP`, with distinct text or structural treatments in scoped rules in `src/style.css`. Show historical author and date fields and preserve the authored lines. Render handle, authored text, and input feedback through text nodes. Keep the prompt, controls, and log usable after rerendering. Dispose the terminal on exit and return focus to the hub prompt.
6. **Wire the app and prove the journeys.** In `src/app/tools.ts`, add `onBbsConnect` to `ToolContext` and have `buildTools` append `CONNECT TO BBS` after the current utilities when `findBbsOffer` returns a board. In `src/main.ts`, implement the callback by checking the current game facts, passing game archives and save-backed progress to `connectBbs`, and calling `scenes.show(createBbsScene(...))`. Use the existing `showHub` callback on disconnect. Apply and persist progress through the existing save session upon login/read, retain in-memory progress if storage refuses the write, and surface that storage result in the BBS. Keep the current hub menu refresh local to its terminal when a tool switches scenes. Add `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` with keyboard and pointer journeys and extend `tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts` to check the offer before and after the actual ending.

## HANDOFF

### Entry points and dependencies

| Area | Approved-base entry points | Planned files and symbols |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authored board | `docs/game-design.md:96`, `content/archives/lore-last-sysop.json:2`, `docs/content-authoring.md:68` | New `content/bbs/relay-07.json`. Update the content authoring guide. Preserve the original farewell and game design. |
| Content | `src/content/schema.ts:129` (`archiveSchema`), `src/content/schema.ts:207` (`Content`), `src/content/validate.ts:42` (`SCHEMAS`), `src/content/validate.ts:60` (`loadContent`), `src/content/validate.ts:149` (`checkReferences`) | Add `bbsMessageSchema`, `bbsBoardSchema`, and `BbsBoard`. Register the board kind and validate conditions and archive references. |
| Persistence | `src/progress/save.ts:29` (`handleSchema`), `src/progress/save.ts:37` (`saveSchema`), `src/progress/save.ts:72` (`freshSave`), `src/progress/save.ts:138` (`loadSave`), `src/progress/save.ts:204` (`openSaveSession`) | Extract `normalizeHandle` and add defaulted `bbsReadMessages`. The app consumes the existing persistence session. |
| Pure session | `src/content/conditions.ts:15` (`evaluate`), `src/puzzle/game.ts:68` (`facts`), `src/puzzle/game.ts:107` (`archives`) | New `src/bbs/bbs.ts` with `findBbsOffer`, `connectBbs`, and `dispatchBbs`. |
| View | `src/app/scenes.ts:1` (`Scene`), `src/terminal/terminal.ts:7` (`Terminal`), `src/terminal/terminal.ts:19` (`createTerminal`), `src/style.css:173` (.terminal) | New `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts` with `createBbsScene`. Add the optional prompt and tones in the terminal and add BBS-scoped styling. |
| App | `src/main.ts:22` (save session), `src/main.ts:104` (`showHub`), `src/main.ts:109` (`toolContext`), `src/app/tools.ts:17` (`ToolContext`), `src/app/tools.ts:145` (`buildTools`), `src/app/hub.ts:22` (tool dispatch) | Modify `toolContext`, `ToolContext`, and `buildTools`. Use the existing scene manager, hub dispatch, and ending callback. |

### Tests and verification

- Add `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`. Extend `tests/unit/content.test.ts:23` (schema fixtures), `tests/unit/content.test.ts:202` (diagnostics), `tests/unit/save.test.ts:36` (save round trips), `tests/unit/helpers.ts:3` (typed fixture), and `tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts:19` (actual episode completion). Reuse `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json` and the patterns in `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts:85` (temporary copy), `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18` (Pages fixture), and `tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts:9` (seed once).
- Run these focused commands on the implementation with prepared dependencies. Role responsibilities and evidence requirements are in [TEST_PLAN.md](TEST_PLAN.md).

```sh
npm test -- tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/episode.test.ts
npm run content:validate
./node_modules/.bin/prettier --check content/bbs/relay-07.json docs/content-authoring.md src/app/tools.ts src/bbs src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts src/main.ts src/progress/save.ts src/style.css src/terminal/terminal.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/helpers.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts
./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/app/tools.ts src/bbs src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts src/main.ts src/progress/save.ts src/terminal/terminal.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/helpers.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
npm run test:e2e -- --list tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts
```

- Browser-enabled verification for the changed specs is `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts`. The existing workflow runs `npm run test:e2e` for the complete browser suite.
- Checked on the provided approved-base snapshot by inspecting file paths and call sites. All five planned new implementation and test files are absent. The worktree snapshot exposes no Git metadata. The actual banner, farewell, v2 codec, literal v1 completion fixture, common hub entry point, and workflow discovery pattern were checked in source. The harness metadata declares issue #25 as a dependency, and this snapshot contains the v2 save foundation the plan needs. `.swarm/active/workunit.json:6`, `src/progress/save.ts:3`.
- Reopen the plan if the implementation base lacks the v2 codec or its migration fixture, if the completion fact or approved Chapter 2 text changed, or if approval is needed for a design beyond the protected harness or first-contact boundary. A browser result pending in CI is expected during sandbox validation.

### What this change breaks

| Existing dependency found in the repository | Treatment |

| `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts:23`, `tests/e2e/settings.spec.ts:137`, `tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts:97`, and `tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts:90` assert or use `OBS>`. `src/app/hub.ts:19` is the only approved-base terminal constructor call. | Preserve the default label and echo, old tool ordering, and command semantics. Add offer assertions to the Episode 000 spec. |
| `tests/unit/episode.test.ts:129` uses `bbs.keel` as an Archive search result. `src/app/tools.ts:101` grants archive reads. `src/world/archive-view.ts:75` has the Archive banner. | Preserve these Archive behaviors. The referenced farewell is `lore.last-sysop`, and BBS reads have their own progress field. |
| `docs/content-authoring.md:73` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/propose-archive-entry.yml:2` describe BBS messages as Archive content. `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts:85` extracts the first authoring example. | Document the new board index by the existing content kinds. Preserve the Archive template and the first worked example unchanged. |
| `docs/architecture.md:31`, `scripts/content-plugin.ts:11`, and `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:25` describe or use shared loading and discovery. | Preserve JSON globbing, build and CLI entry points, Pages fixtures, and workflow discovery unchanged. |

# ISSUE-26 test plan

Exercise the real content loader, save codec, hub tool list, and pure BBS dispatcher in Node. Use the existing Pages fixture to verify browser interactions, rendering, and persistence. Numbering follows the seven checkboxes in the [WorkUnit](WORKUNIT.md#acceptance-criteria).

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Cases and observable results | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Node coverage of the BBS session | Use the loaded board and public BBS API to connect and assert the full banner in order and the login phase. Exercise custom `LOGIN <handle>` and `DESIGNATION` in separate sessions. Verify trim, case and length behavior, blank input, and the custom path with no designation. After login verify the main menu, message index, displayed Keel record, SYSOP greeting, return to the menu, and disconnect. Exercise `HELP` in each interactive phase and unknown or unavailable input, including a read before login and an unknown message ID. Verify that invalid actions do not change progress and reopening the same message does not add a second read key. | `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts` via **Node**. |
| 2. Typed and clickable controls with visible hints | In the keyboard journey, also type `HELP` at login and in the message index, use `SYSOP` and `MENU`, and reconnect once to submit `LOGIN <handle>`. In the pointer journey, use the offer button, labelled custom-handle form and submit button, message index, individual message button, SYSOP, menu, help, and disconnect controls. Exercise the designation button in a second login. At login and after login, assert visible hints for the actions available in that phase. Check that command and click routes enter the same dispatcher, including disconnect at login. | `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` via **Browser** and tester source review. |
| 3. Distinct message presentation | In the same browser journey, assert the visible `SYSTEM`, `HISTORICAL MESSAGE`, and `SYSOP` labels alongside their actual content. Verify the five system banner lines as displayed in order, the historical title, author and date with the farewell, and a separate SYSOP block. Check BBS-scoped styles for distinct structural or typographic treatments. At a narrow viewport, use the visible controls and prompt and confirm that the labels are readable without depending on colour. | `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` via **Browser** and tester source review of `src/style.css` and `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts`. |
| 4. Completion gate and v1 migration | Invoke the actual `buildTools` entry point with a fresh or incomplete save, a completed current save without FORGE flags, and `openSaveSession` loaded from `episode-000-complete-v1.json`. Verify offer counts of zero, one, and one, and confirm the pure connect path refuses an incomplete save. The existing Episode 000 browser journey checks absence on join and presence after the real ending and `CONTINUE`. The seeded keyboard journey verifies that the migrated save can use the offer. | `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts`, `tests/unit/save.test.ts`, and `tests/unit/episode.test.ts` via **Node**. `tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` via **Browser**. |
| 5. Persistence and return to the hub | Round-trip a normalized handle and a board-scoped read key through the supported codec. Read existing v2 bytes with the BBS field absent and assert `loaded` with an empty history. Assert initialized BBS data on migration while comparing prior progress and designation. In the browser, log in with a custom handle and read the farewell, reload without reseeding, rejoin and reconnect, then assert the prefilled handle and retained read marker. Disconnect and confirm focus on `OBS>`, use `STATUS` to inspect the handle, and open the existing `ARCHIVE` tool to verify it remains functional. Review the write path for local-only persistence and plain-text rendering. | `tests/unit/save.test.ts` via **Node** and `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` via **Browser**. |
| 6. Keyboard journey in the existing workflow | Seed the untouched completed v1 fixture into `signal-lost.save` before the first navigation. With the existing `fixtures.ts` and Pages base, press Enter to join and type `CONNECT TO BBS`, `DESIGNATION`, `MESSAGES`, `READ lore.last-sysop`, and `DISCONNECT` with Enter. Assert the banner, migrated designation, opened historical message, and restored hub prompt. Discover the spec with Playwright before CI runs it. | `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` via **Discovery** and the **Browser tests** workflow. |
| 7. JSON-only extension in a temporary copy | Copy `content/` recursively into a temporary directory as in the authoring test. Write a new eligible Archive JSON record and append its ID to the copied board index. Pass the temporary copy through `readContentDir` and `loadContent`, checking no diagnostics and a manifest entry for the new record. Connect with the loaded result, then verify that the index lists the new title and `READ <new-id>` opens its body. Clean up in `finally`. In schema tests, assert file and field for an invalid board field, an unknown or repeated archive reference, and an unknown completion fact. | `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts` and `tests/unit/content.test.ts` via **Node**. **Content** validates the shipped tree. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Run these commands on the implemented candidate with prepared repository dependencies. Record the command, candidate or source snapshot, result, and any unresolved failure or coverage gap.

```

```

## Tester-owned independent review and result reuse

- Trace all seven acceptance criteria from the app entry points to the tests. Check that the completion gate consults saved facts through the same path used during live play, that the v1 fixture enters through the real migration, and that the temporary-content case reads through the actual BBS dispatcher.
- Inspect the click and typed paths, prompt focus after transitions, message labels, scope of CSS, and use of text nodes. Check historical text against its source and compare the five-line banner with the approved design. Confirm the custom handle and read keys reach the save session and that no network or account code handles them. Confirm disconnect mounts the normal hub tools and the protected paths are outside the implementation changes.
- Reuse applicable passing developer results for the same relevant sources. Repeat only checks affected by a relevant source change, an observed failure, or an unresolved coverage concern. Use the focused commands above to address specific gaps and record the reason and result.
- Record browser discovery and source-review evidence separately from Chromium outcomes. When the role sandbox cannot run Chromium, report the runtime result as pending until CI evidence is available. A discovered test proves registration. The PR workflow provides the browser results required before merge.

### Required revision

**F1. Make Episode 000 completion mandatory for every BBS offer and connection.** Steps 1–4 of [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) put the completion predicate in the shipped JSON and use the shared condition evaluator. The proposed reference check only confirms that referenced facts exist. For example, `{"not":"completed:episode.000"}` refers to a valid episode and evaluates to true for a fresh save. Under the proposed checks, that board could appear early and admit a connection. Require the completion predicate in the board schema, or apply a mandatory completion check to both runtime entry points. Add a distinguishing case in [TEST_PLAN.md](TEST_PLAN.md) using a board conditioned on the absence of completion. Verify rejection at the authored field, or verify that both offer and direct connection refuse it before completion. Keep the existing completed and migrated-save cases. [Condition evaluation](../../src/content/conditions.ts#L15) · [Reference validation](../../src/content/validate.ts#L166)
